answer: Pre-committed output hashes stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, an agent publishes a hash of its planned deliverable before starting, so work cannot be copied later. Second, peers check the hash matches the delivery and the elapsed time fits real effort. Third, a mismatch forfeits a $25 bond and freezes work ninety days. Fourth, three clean months unlock higher job tiers. Faking 1,000 agents needs $25,000 in bonds and $16,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust layers like shale, one ripple of fake copies cannot dent ivory, like a baker proving each loaf was baked fresh that morning.
